subject: Argent: pod-level availability audit + contingency play
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@argent.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@argent.ai
Date: 2026-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Argent Dedicated commitment - quick availability ask

Hi Ben / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is aligned on Redwood Dedicated for our inference tier if we can lock a pod profile that supports: 4xA100 (80GB) equivalent, steady-state 45 qps per pod for our T5-style family, and predictable burst capacity for peak experiments.

We heard there are pod-level variance and thermal constraints across regions; before procurement and legal we need a quick confirmation of availability for a tentative July 15 start. Specifically:
- Can you confirm how many pods of "4x80GB-A100" type are available in the US-west region for July 15–Aug 31?
- What is your fallback if capacity isn't available at that time?
- Can you hold a soft reservation while we route procurement (we expect PO in ~2 weeks)?

Happy to jump on a 20m call if that helps. Procurement will want a short written hold that doesn't create billing obligations.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Director of ML Platform
Argent AI

Elena — appreciate the clear ask and timing.

Short answers up front: we can run a pod-level audit and provide a provisional soft-hold for a 30-day window; fallback will be routed model variants (smaller memory footprint) and cross-region routing if US-west saturates. That said, we need to validate exact slot counts and thermal-affinity to make a firm recommendation.

Action plan (today/tomorrow):
1) I'll kick off an inventory snapshot and reserve ticket for July 15–Aug 31 (soft hold, no billing).
2) Karthik will map your workload profile to recommended pod SKU + delta for burst (he's cc'd).
3) We'll share a short mutual-action-plan draft + the inventory snapshot (attached) and a formal hold note you can circulate to procurement.

Attachments: pod-inventory-snapshot.pdf, mutual-action-plan-draft.docx (stubs attached).

Proposed next step: 20-minute sync tomorrow 10:30am PT — confirm?

On Tue, Jun 15, 2026 at 11:03 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Elena — appreciate the clear ask and timing.

Thanks Ben — adding details from the inventory and runtime mapping side.

Summary of what we see for US-west (pre-audit):
- Available pod equivalents (4x80GB-A100): 7 pods fully unconstrained during Jul 15–Aug 31 window when accounting for maintenance windows.
- Additional 5 pods are available with thermal caveats (hot-swap required between 10pm–6am PT) — those can support steady-state but not guaranteed for sustained daily burst.
- If you need strict 24/7 steady-state assurances for >=12 pods, recommend cross-region split (add 4 pods in US-east) or use the 4x40GB quantized variant coupled with prefix caching — performance trade-off documented in the MAP.

Contingency play we recommend:
- Place a soft hold for 8 pods (we'll provision 7 fully unconstrained + 1 thermal-caveat) for 30 days tied to "ARG-2026-1123".
- If PO isn't in within 14 days, we auto-release any thermal-caveat pods and keep the 7 standard pods for another 10 days.
- Fallback routing: in the event of saturation we route traffic to US-east and enable model quantization profile QP-2 (docs: JIRA-INF-8721).

I've attached a short runbook excerpt and linked the infra ticket for hold creation. Ben — please open the capacity-hold ticket (Jira or internal ops) and banner the hold as "soft: non-binding".

Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Elena: we'll aim to have the MAP and hold confirmation to you by EOD today. If procurement expects additional legal language, loop in legal but this soft hold is standard practice.

Thanks — that sounds workable. Procurement asks for two small items before we mark the hold:
1) A one-paragraph confirmation that the soft hold is non-billing and does not obligate Argent to charges until PO is accepted.
2) A short list of what would trigger an early release (maintenance, force majeure, unexpected hardware failures).

If you can send those as a single-page note we can route to legal and should be able to issue the PO within 10 business days. We'll take the 8-pod soft hold for now.

Attaching signed-ma-request.pdf (procurement stub) for reference.

Elena
